channel.title: Rambam's Hilchot Teshuvah — Dayan Daniel Kada
channel.description: Dayan Daniel Kada's series on the Rambam's Laws of Repentance: what teshuvah is, confession, free will and the World to Come.
channel.itunes:author: Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: Teshuvah Is Not the Misvah: Why the Rambam Begins with Viduy | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 1
item.description:
Why does the Rambam make viduy, not teshuvah, the misvah? Hilchot Teshuvah 1: teshuvah as returning to what one was always obliged to do, leaving the sin in present, past and future, viduy as restoring the relationship and why it must be spoken and specific, and the levels of atonement.
Notes based on the transcript - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sn9rLHFnk3tGYhcioBQbNZAxxXDxhuTt9rB-m6w6PhU/edit?usp=sharing

item.title: Complete Teshuvah: Letting the Old Self Die | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 2
item.description:
What makes teshuvah complete? Hilchot Teshuvah 2: meeting the same situation and not sinning because one has become someone else, letting the old self die, emotional and intellectual routes, spoken and specific viduy, the paths of teshuvah, Yom Kippur, and making amends between people.

item.title: Rosh Hashanah Weighs Who You Are, Not What You Did | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 3
item.description:
What does Rosh Hashanah actually weigh? Hilchot Teshuvah 3: merits and sins measured by magnitude, the problems with a simple tally, the answer that judgment weighs identity and values rather than acts, what being sealed for life means, and the wake-up call of the shofar.

item.title: He Passes Them Over One by One: Fragmented Sins & Losing Olam HaBa | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 3
item.description:
How are repeated sins weighed, and who loses a share in Olam HaBa? Hilchot Teshuvah 3: sins passed over one by one, a share for every Jew and for the righteous of the nations, the 24 who have none, corporeality as heresy, habitual lesser sins, and nothing standing before teshuvah.

item.title: What Blocks Teshuvah? The 24 Impediments & the Sins We Don't Notice | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 4
item.description:
What stands in the way of teshuvah? The 24 impediments of Hilchot Teshuvah 4 in five categories, from causing the public to sin to habits like lashon hara and temper, why the worst concern influence on others, why rebuke works only from friendship, and why none finally prevents teshuvah.

item.title: Free Will & God's Knowledge: We Must Know We're Free, Not How | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 5
item.description:
If God knows what we will do, are we free? Hilchot Teshuvah 5: every person can be righteous or wicked, nothing decrees who we become, astrology has no influence, and since God's knowledge is one with Him and beyond our grasp, we must know that we are free, not how.

item.title: When God Hardens a Heart: Pharaoh, Addiction & the Loss of Teshuvah | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 6
item.description:
Can a person lose the ability to do teshuvah? Hilchot Teshuvah 6: how consequences come, teshuvah as a shield, and Pharaoh's hardened heart read like addiction, with the readings of Rav Saadiah, the Ramban and the Rambam, what guiding sinners means, and the responsibility of the Egyptians.

item.title: The Love of Teshuvah & the Meaning of Karet | Hilchot Teshuvah Perakim 7–8
item.description:
The love of teshuvah in Hilchot Teshuvah 7: do it now, change character and not only deeds, the place of the baal teshuvah, and never shaming anyone for their past. Then chapter 8 opens with Olam HaBa as life without death, karet as being cut off, and no reincarnation in the Rambam's thought.

item.title: What Is Olam HaBa? Crowns of Knowledge & the Shechinah's Splendour | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 8
item.description:
What is Olam HaBa? Hilchot Teshuvah 8 describes an existence without bodies: the crowns of the righteous are the knowledge they acquired, and enjoying the Shekhinah means grasping HaShem as one cannot in a body. Also karet, death by the hand of Heaven, and why resurrection is not Olam HaBa.

item.title: Olam HaBa Is Already Here: Mashiah & the Resurrection Puzzle | Hilchot Teshuvah Perek 8
item.description:

item.title: Serving from Love: Why the Torah Promises Rain, Not Olam HaBa | Hilchot Teshuvah Perakim 9–10
item.description:
If Olam HaBa is the real reward, why does the Torah promise rain and plenty? The close of Hilchot Teshuvah: blessings in this world are bonuses that motivate us and free us to serve, why the wicked may prosper, what the Rambam means by hedonism, and serving HaShem from love.
